<reason>B made the stronger comparative case by defending narrowly controlled public-interest access rather than abusive commercial sales. A’s autonomy and irreversible-disclosure concerns remained relevant, but its claim that this access fell outside the motion collapsed. A then asserted that planning losses were marginal while repeatedly overlooking B’s preventive safeguards. B answered the pressure directly and better explained why the additional consent requirement needed justification even where both sides supported strong protections.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B forced A to concede that paid access inside a secure environment was covered by the prohibition, then challenged A’s remaining comparison: access need not create another downloadable copy, and evacuation-model omissions affect people, not merely spreadsheets. This directly weakened both A’s scope defense and its weighing.</best_rebuttal>
